summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for in-stent restenosis of the right transplanted renal artery, presenting with elevated blood pressure. A transplant kidney ultrasound revealed significantly increased renal artery velocities, confirming restenosis. The patient underwent an elective angioplasty of the existing renal artery stent via endovascular approach using CO2 contrast, with no complications. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout, with preserved renal function post-procedure. Pain was controlled, and he tolerated advancement of diet and activity. He was discharged home on dual antiplatelet therapy, antihypertensives, immunosuppressants, and insulin, with instructions for wound care, activity restrictions, and follow-up with vascular surgery and transplant nephrology.
